"Ar module pilot Ken Mattingly, in an interview for the Apollo 13 mission, claimed that the film portrayed his character, Jack Swigert, as unprepared for the flight. However, this was untrue, as Swigert was very familiar with the module, having also worked on its development. The dialogue between ground control and the astronauts in the film was taken nearly verbatim from transcripts and recordings, with the exception of the famous line 'Houston, we have a problem.' According to audio of the air-to-ground communications, the actual words uttered by Swigert were 'Okay, Houston, we've had a problem here.' Ground control responded by saying, 'This is Houston. Say again, please.' Jim Lovell then repeated, 'Houston, we've had a problem.'

One other incorrect dialogue in the film is after the re-entry blackout. In the actual re-entry, the Command Module's transmission was not met with a response from ground control, as depicted in the film. Instead, the module was able to re-establish communication on its own.

In the film, there is also a dramatized scene in which the astronauts experience a sense of weightlessness and floating within the spacecraft. However, in reality, the sensation of weightlessness in space is not accompanied by the visual effects depicted in the film.

Cainan is included between Arphaxad and Shelah, following the Septuagint text (though not included in the Masoretic Text followed by most modern Bibles). Augustine notes that the count of generations in the Book of Luke is 77, a number symbolizing the forgiveness of all sins.
